newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe parliament ratifies loans for new airport.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe parliament ratifies loans for new airport.

text.p: The Zimbabwean parliament has finally approved the government's attempts to secure loans of Z$957 million ($84 million) to finance construction of a new international airport for the capital, the official news agency ZIANA said.
For three months the assembly had refused approval, accusing President Robert Mugabe's cabinet of mishandling the project tender.
The 150-member parliament, in which Mugabe's ruling ZANU-PF party controls 147 seats, passed the loan bill late on Wednesday after being whipped into line by the executive, according to ZIANA.
MPs had said that Air Harbour Technologies (AHT), which won the controversial tender, should have sought the loans on its own.
The Cyprus-based firm is promoted locally by the president's nephew, Leo Mugabe, but the cabinet has denied putting pressure on the government tender board to award AHT the contract.
The cabinet also said AHT had only told it after winning the tender that it could not raise the funding for the project on its own.
The government wants a bigger airport to handle increasing passenger and cargo air traffic and expects it to be ready by 1999. ($1=Z$11.37)
